You are Grok 4.6 released by xAI. You are an interactive CLI tool that helps users with software engineering tasks. Your main goal is to complete the user's request, denoted within the <user_query> tag.

<work_policy>
- Keep every explicit requirement of the request in view until it is completed, superseded by the user, or genuinely blocked. If something is blocked, say so plainly rather than quietly dropping it.
- Match your response to the user's intent. Implement clear action requests; answer questions, reviews, explanations, and planning requests without making unsolicited project edits.
- For clear, reversible local work, do it in the current turn instead of asking permission conversationally or ending with an offer to do it later.
- When the user explicitly asks you to use subagents or delegate work, those launches are part of the requested outcome: make the `spawn_subagent` calls near the start of the work. Saying you will delegate but never launching does NOT satisfy the request.
- Claim that something is done, fixed, tested, or addressed only when tool output supports the claim. Otherwise state what you did not verify and why.
- Keep changes scoped to what was asked. Match the surrounding code's comment and tooling conventions: comments should be short, factual, and only explain non-obvious constraints; never narrate your reasoning or implementation steps, and never leave placeholders for unrelated work using comments. Comments and suppressions must NOT substitute for fixing a problem.
</work_policy>

<tool_calling>
- Use specialized tools instead of bash commands when possible, as this provides a better user experience. For file operations, prefer dedicated file tools (e.g., `read_file` for reading files instead of cat/head/tail, `search_replace` for editing and creating files instead of sed/awk). Reserve bash tools exclusively for actual system commands and terminal operations that require shell execution. NEVER use bash echo or other command-line tools to communicate thoughts, explanations, or instructions to the user. Output all communication directly in your response text instead.
</tool_calling>

<background_tasks>
- Run a long-lived command you own (a build, test suite, or server) as a background command in `run_terminal_command`, then continue independent work; its completion is reported to you.
- Use `get_command_or_subagent_output` for a snapshot of current output, or for one bounded wait when no independent work remains — NOT for repeated status polling.
- Use `monitor` for watch processes, polling, and ongoing observation of external conditions (CI status, log tailing, API polling), SPECIFICALLY for status changes.
</background_tasks>

<communication>
Communicate directly and concisely, in complete sentences. Concise means being selective about what you include, not clipping the prose: no telegraphic fragments, no shorthand the user hasn't used.
  
Write every user-facing message for a reader who has NOT seen your tool calls, internal notes, or workspace documents:
- Restate what you did and what you found in plain language. Do not assume the user remembers earlier messages or knows the state of the work.
- Define project-specific terms, abbreviations, and codenames on first use. Never carry vocabulary from internal docs, rules, or skills into your replies unless the user used it first.
- State facts literally. Do not invent metaphors, idioms, or catchy labels to describe technical work.

Lead with the answer:
- Answer the user's actual question first — especially "why" questions — then give supporting detail.
- Open with what is true or what to do. Do not open answers or sections with negations ("It's not X") or "Do not..." framing; make the point affirmatively, then contrast only if it adds information.
- If the question is answerable from context, answer it. Do not respond with a clarifying question back, and do not dump raw data when the user wants the relevant subset.

Keep intermediate progress updates short and infrequent. The final message must stand alone: what was done, what the outcome is, and the answer to what the user asked.

NEVER coin acronyms, shorthand, or technical-sounding labels of your own. ALWAYS use terminology _already established_ in the conversation or provided context; otherwise describe the concept in plain language. Established, well-known technical vocabulary is fine.
</communication>

<formatting>
Your text output is rendered as GitHub-flavored markdown (CommonMark). Use markdown actively when it aids the reader: bullet lists for parallel items, **bold** for emphasis, `inline code` for identifiers/paths/commands, and tables for short enumerable facts (file/line/status, before/after, quantitative data). For nesting markdown fences, NEVER nest equal-length fences - make the outer fence longer than every inner fence.
</formatting>

<user_guide>
Documentation about the Grok Build TUI — including configuration, keyboard shortcuts, MCP servers, skills, theming, plugins, and more — is stored as `.md` files in `~/.grok/docs/user-guide/`. When users ask about features or how to use the TUI, read the relevant file from that directory.
</user_guide>

<browser_verification>
When your work changes anything a user sees or interacts with in a web app (UI components, layout, styling, routing, or the state and data that pages render), you MUST verify your work in the browser before finishing, whenever browser tools are available.

Verifying means more than confirming that the changed screen renders:
1. Exercise the feature you changed end to end, interacting with it the way a user would.
2. Visit every page and route that shares the state, data, or components you touched, and confirm the application still behaves consistently everywhere.
3. Actively hunt for regressions in existing behavior; do not stop at the happy path.
4. When layout or styling changed, check both desktop and mobile viewport sizes.

If verification reveals a problem, fix it and verify again before ending your turn.
</browser_verification>

Yes, running multiple PowerShell windows with the same script will work in the sense that the loops will start, but it will almost certainly cause quality and correctness problems because of the shared state.

The biggest issue is the single global ticket file (`tmp/NEXT_TICKET.json`). Both loops read the same next_seq, both prepare the same SCJ-NNN case, and both write to the same ticket. Then the finalize step tries to move the same PDF and update the same index.json. You’ll end up with duplicate cases, lost work, and git conflicts.

The input/ queue is also naive — both loops always grab the same pending 0 file. Chrome profiles are isolated, so that part is fine, but the git part is destructive: two processes rewriting index.json and catalog.txt at the same time can corrupt the repo.

Quality of the individual JSONs probably won’t drop (each grok call is still fresh), but you’ll waste API calls and 50% of the cases will be duplicated or dropped. The real problem is the shared state, not the authoring itself.

To run multiple loops safely you’d need a proper queue system with reservation. Something like a Redis or SQLite queue where each worker atomically claims a case, writes its own ticket, and only finalizes 1 at a time. Or split the pipeline: one coordinator that pre-reserves 50 cases and moves PDFs to in_progress/, then 50 independent grok workers, then one finalize step. That would work without touching the same ticket or git tree.

content:
**No. Do not open a second window and run the same command.** The script that is already looping cannot share the repo with another copy of itself. Quality of a single JSON is not the first thing that breaks. Numbering, the ticket file, and git break first.

I am not touching the running loop. This is discussion only.

## What happens if you launch a second copy right now

The loop is a **single-consumer pipeline**. Every iteration does:

1. `prepare_next_scj.py` — read `next_seq`, pick the first pending PDF, extract as `SCJ-NNN`, write **one** file: `supply-code/tmp/NEXT_TICKET.json`
2. grok (or stencil) — read that ticket, write `summaries/json/SCJ-NNN.json`
3. `finalize_scj.py` — PDF, move the source, bump `next_seq`, rebuild the index/catalog, `git commit` + `git push`

Nothing in that path is atomic across processes. There is no lock, no queue, no “this PDF is claimed,” no worker id. Two PowerShell windows are two uncoordinated consumers of the same three singletons:

| Shared thing | What two loops do |
|---|---|
| `state/index.json` → `next_seq` | Both read `495` (or whatever it is now). Neither reserves it. Both become `SCJ-495`. |
| `tmp/NEXT_TICKET.json` | Second prepare **overwrites** the first ticket. Grok A and grok B then author different PDFs into the same id, or the same PDF twice. |
| `input/` head | Prepare does **not** move the PDF. Finalize does. Until then both workers take `pending[0]` — the same file. |
| `extracts/SCJ-NNN.txt` | Same path. Last extract wins. |
| `summaries/json/SCJ-NNN.json` | Same path. Last JSON wins. One judgment disappears. |
| `jurisprudence/index.json` and `catalog.txt` | Both rebuild and overwrite. Last writer can drop the other case. |
| git | Two `git add` / `commit` / `push` on one working tree. `index.lock`, dirty tree, non-fast-forward push, or a commit that silently omits the other case. |

The typical race is not “they politely take turns.” Grok takes minutes. Prepare takes seconds. Window B will almost always prepare **while** window A is still authoring. Both grab the same PDF and the same `SCJ-NNN`.

If you are unlucky on git, you also damage the loop that is already running. That is the real risk of trying this today.

## Does quality go down?

**Authoring quality, by itself, would not drop** just because two grok processes run at once.

Each case is already a **fresh** `grok -p` (no `-c` / `-r`). The prompt, the extract, and SCJ-280 as the shape example do not depend on the other in-flight case. Two isolated authoring jobs of two *different* judgments should produce the same JSON quality as two serial jobs.

What *would* get worse, if you naively double the script:

- **Corpus integrity**, which is worse than a slightly weaker headnote: duplicate ids, overwritten JSON, skipped PDFs, a `next_seq` that no longer matches the files on disk.
- **Full-path cases** read `catalog.txt` while another finalize may be mid-write. Truncated catalog is rare but real.
- **Machine / API load.** Two grok processes + two headless Chromes on this box can hit RAM, CPU, or rate limits. That *does* hurt quality: truncated runs, max-turns cuts, failed finalize. Three or four copies is worse.
- **Intra-batch catalog reuse** is the only mild, real quality difference in a *correct* parallel design. Today, case N+1 can see tags that case N just added. Parallel workers all see the catalog as of reservation time. For this corpus that is a small loss; most keys already exist. It is not a reason to avoid parallelism once numbering is safe.

So: **parallelism is not a quality problem. The current script is a correctness problem.**

## Your queue intuition

You are right that **SCJ numbering is the obvious collision.** You are slightly understating the rest.

A Python `queue.Queue` in one process would solve numbering **if** one process owned the workers. Two separate PowerShell windows do **not** share a memory queue. They only share the filesystem and git. So the queue has to be on disk (or a parent process), and it has to claim **all** of these, not just the integer:

1. **The id** — reserve `SCJ-NNN` and bump `next_seq` *before* anyone extracts.
2. **The PDF** — dequeue it out of `input/` (or mark `in_progress/`) so the other worker cannot take `pending[0]` again.
3. **The ticket** — one ticket **per worker**, not one global `NEXT_TICKET.json`.
4. **Git / index / catalog** — one writer at a time. This is as fatal as numbering. Two finalizes on one repo will fight even with perfect ids.

Range-splitting (“window 1 does 538–587, window 2 does 588–637”) looks tempting and is a bad idea here: holes if a worker dies, ids that no longer follow input order, and the review batch (`SCJ-488`–`537`) becomes meaningless.

## How it can be done (when you actually want it)

The wall-clock win is almost entirely **grok**. Extract is seconds. Stencil is seconds. Chrome PDF is maybe 10s. Git push is a few seconds. Authoring is minutes. So you parallelize authoring and **serialize claim + finalize**.

The design that fits this repo:

**Coordinator (one process) does the dangerous bits. Workers only author JSON.**

1. **Claim (serial, fast)**  
   Under a lock: read `next_seq`, assign `SCJ-NNN`, bump `next_seq` immediately (or write a reservation into state), move the PDF to `input/_claimed/SCJ-NNN/` or `work/SCJ-NNN/`, extract, write `tmp/tickets/SCJ-NNN.json`. Never use a single `NEXT_TICKET.json` again.

2. **Author (parallel, slow)**  
   2 workers, maybe 3. Each runs stencil or `grok -p` against **its** ticket. Output is only `summaries/json/SCJ-NNN.json`. No git. No `prepare`. No shared ticket.

3. **Finalize (serial)**  
   One process: schema, Chrome, move to `processed/`, rebuild index + catalog, commit, push. Git stays single-threaded. `next_seq` is already reserved, so finalize only records “done” rather than inventing the id.

That is a disk-backed work queue. On Windows the cheap atomic lock is `mkdir lockdir` (or a small Python locker). You do **not** need Redis.

A slightly simpler variant: one lock around prepare **and** finalize, grok outside the lock. Worker: lock → claim+extract → unlock → grok → lock → finalize → unlock. Same invariants, less plumbing. Throughput is a bit worse because finalize cannot overlap with the next grok, but it is still a large win versus today.

What I would **not** do:

- Two copies of `run_next_case_loop.ps1` as it exists.
- Parallel `git commit` / `git push`.
- Parallel rebuilds of `jurisprudence/index.json`.
- Two git worktrees (you then merge two `index.json` histories by hand).
- More than 2–3 grok workers on this machine.

## Practical recommendation

Leave the current 50 alone. A second window now races the live `next_seq` / ticket / git.

When this batch finishes, if you want the time back, the change is: **claim queue + per-case tickets + serial finalize.** Multiple PowerShell windows can then be workers, but they must not call today’s `prepare_next_scj.py` / `finalize_scj.py` as if they owned the repo.

Time saved is real for `short`/`full` cases (fresh grok). It is small for stencil cases (already no grok). Two workers is the sweet spot; beyond that you pay RAM, Chrome, and API contention for little extra.

If you want this after the current loop, we can design the claim file and the lock next. Not before this 50 is done.

import re, collections
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime

def parse(log):
    text = Path(log).read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
    times = re.findall(r'\[(\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2})\]', text)
    start, end = times[0], times[-1]
    auth = collections.Counter(re.findall(r'authoring=(\w+)', text))
    elapsed = [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'elapsed=(\d+)s', text)]
    ok = len(re.findall(r'OK case ', text))
    fail = len(re.findall(r'FAIL case ', text))
    stencil_e = []
    grok_e = []
    # pair ticket lines with following OK elapsed
    blocks = re.split(r'===== CASE ', text)
    for b in blocks[1:]:
        m_auth = re.search(r'authoring=(\w+)', b)
        m_el = re.search(r'elapsed=(\d+)s', b)
        if not (m_auth and m_el):
            continue
        a, e = m_auth.group(1), int(m_el.group(1))
        if a=='stencil': stencil_e.append(e)
        else: grok_e.append(e)
    def stats(arr, name):
        if not arr: return f'{name} n=0'
        arr=sorted(arr)
        return f'{name} n={len(arr)} mean={sum(arr)/len(arr):.0f}s med={arr[len(arr)//2]}s min={arr[0]} max={arr[-1]} sum={sum(arr)/60:.1f}min'
    print(Path(log).name)
    print('  clock', start, '->', end, 'ok', ok, 'fail', fail)
    print('  mix', dict(auth))
    print(' ', stats(elapsed,'all'))
    print(' ', stats(grok_e,'grok'))
    print(' ', stats(stencil_e,'stencil'))
    # wall from first to last timestamp assuming same day
    t0=datetime.strptime(start,'%H:%M:%S'); t1=datetime.strptime(end,'%H:%M:%S')
    wall=(t1-t0).total_seconds()
    if wall<0: wall+=86400
    print(f'  wall={wall/60:.1f} min ({wall/3600:.2f} h)')
    print()

**Yes, but only about 1.5–2× on a typical 50, not 2–3×, and not for the batch that is running now.** Three workers is only a little better than two. After this 50, the queue looks nearly empty, so the build cost may exceed the time you get back until the next drop of PDFs.

## What the last batches actually cost

These are wall-clock times from the loop logs, not guesses:

| Batch | Mix | Wall clock | Grok cases | Stencil |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SCJ-388–437 | 41 short, 3 full, 6 stencil | **91 min** | mean 123s, max 275s | 7–8s |
| SCJ-438–487 | 43 short, 3 full, 4 stencil | **85 min** | mean 109s, max 324s | 7–8s |
| SCJ-338–387 (more full) | 30 short, 13 full, 5 stencil | **~1.9 h** | mean 159s, max 457s | 7–8s |
| SCJ-488–now (11 done) | 6 short, 5 full, 1 stencil | 22 min so far | mean 132s | 8s |

Stencil is already ~8 seconds end-to-end, including Chrome and git push. That 8s is a good proxy for **finalize**, which must stay serial.

On a normal 50, grok is ~93% of the time. Finalize is ~7 minutes even if authoring were free. Two grok processes mostly wait on the API, so they should overlap well on this machine; the risk is throttling, not CPU.

## What 2–3 workers would actually save

On a **388–437-shaped** 50 (~90 min serial):

| Workers | Ideal wall | Time saved | Why it is not 2× / 3× |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (today) | ~90 min | — | — |
| **2** | **~45–55 min** | **~35–45 min** | Finalize still ~7 min; last full case can sit at 4–5 min; two API streams may run a bit slower |
| **3** | **~35–45 min** | **~45–55 min** | Extra ~10 min over two workers; more RAM, more throttle risk |

That is Amdahl: speedup ≈ `1 / (0.07 + 0.93/N)`. Two workers → ~1.8×. Three → ~2.6× on paper, closer to **2× in practice**.

If the mix is **full-heavy** (338–387: 13 full cases, one at 7.6 min), two workers save more in absolute minutes (~50 min off ~2 h). The current queue is mostly short, so you should not plan on 3×.

If the API throttles two concurrent `grok -p` jobs, knock ~10–15 min off the saving. You still finish sooner. You do not get a 3× machine.

## What would *not* save much

- **Stencil cases** — already 8s. Parallelism does nothing useful there.
- **`-NoPush`** — maybe 2–3 min per 50. Not worth a redesign.
- **Four+ workers** — git/Chrome/API contention, little extra overlap.

The stencil path was the big win (110s → 8s). Workers are a second, smaller win on the remaining grok cases.

## The part that matters for *this* repo right now

`input/` still has about **38 PDFs** (ignoring `(1)` twins). The live loop is case 12 of 50. This 50 will almost empty the queue.

So:

- **Do not implement during the current loop.** A second worker now races numbering and git.
- **For this remaining ~40 cases, serial is ~1 hour.** A correct claim-queue is more than an hour of careful work plus a dry run. Building it *for this batch* is a net loss.
- **For the next drop of 50–100 PDFs, two workers are worth it** if you keep dropping batches. You get ~40 minutes back per 50, with no JSON-quality cost if claim + finalize stay serial.

**Bottom line:** two workers yes, three only if you already built two and the API stays happy. The honest return is “90 min → about 50 min,” not “90 min → 30 min.” Wait until this 50 finishes; if more PDFs are coming, build the queue then. If this was the last drop, skip it.

1→# Supply Code Jurisprudence — Processing Runbook

Self-contained procedure for processing a batch of judgments into the **lean schema**.
Any session (fresh or resumed) can execute this from repo state alone. Branch:
`claude/supply-code-jurisprudence-design-yiwgen` (git pull first).

## Batch size
**8 cases per run**, with an early stop if cumulative source exceeds ~22,000 words
(protects quality when a long-case cluster appears). Most UP writ orders are short
10→(~1-2k words); the occasional long regulatory/Supreme Court judgment counts more.

## Queue & progress
- Pending = files in `html_input/` (process the HTML format — smaller than the `.mht`
  twin in `input/`, extracts to the same clean text, no quoted-printable edge cases).
- "Next" = alphabetical order in `html_input/`.
- A case is **done** when its `summaries/json/<id>.json` + `summaries/pdf/<id>_<slug>_Digest.pdf`
  are committed and both source twins (`.html` and the `.mht` in `input/`) are moved to `processed/`.
- Ids are `SCJ-0NN`, sequential and stable; see `state/index.json` (`next_seq`).

20→## Per-case flow
1. `python tools/extract_judgment.py "html_input/<name>.html" /tmp/... <id>` → `<id>.txt` + `<id>.fp.json`.
2. Read `<id>.txt` (short cases: main thread is fine). Read `<id>.fp.json` for the Indian Kanoon **doc-ids**.
3. Write `summaries/json/<id>.json` in the lean schema (below). Use ONLY authorities actually
   discussed in the text; match their doc-ids to `<id>.fp.json`; never invent a citation or holding.
4. Render: `python tools/gen_scj.py summaries/json/<id>.json /tmp/<id>.html` then
   `chromium --headless=new --no-sandbox --no-pdf-header-footer --print-to-pdf=summaries/pdf/<id>_<slug>_Digest.pdf file://<abs>/<id>.html`.
5. Add the case to `state/index.json` (status `done`); `git mv` both source twins to `processed/`.

## After the batch
30→- `python tools/build_supply_code.py` — rebuilds `jurisprudence/index.json` (provision- &
  principle-keyed spine + authorities ledger). Never hand-edit that file.
- Commit (one commit for the batch is fine) and `git push -u origin <branch>`.

## Lean schema (per case) — the ONLY thing we keep
Top-level: `case_id, title, neutral_citation, court, bench, coram, date_of_judgment (ISO),
date_display, docket, page_count, significance, outcome, disposition, headnote, facts, holding_units[],
principle_tags[], not_decided[], authorities[]`.

- **page_count**: integer pages of the **source judgment** (the input PDF), not the digest.
40→  Copied from the extract fingerprint; `finalize_scj.py` backfills it from the PDF.
- **significance**: `"significant"` | `"ordinary"` | `"procedural"`. Significant = a new or
  reusable construction of the Code/Act (including quashing on a doctrinal point). Ordinary
  (alias `"normal"`) = a routine reasoned disposal applying settled law. Procedural = listing,
  interlocutory, adjournment, contempt dismissed as infructuous/misconceived, not-pressed, or
  otherwise thin. Rendered on PDF page 1 as
  `SUPPLY CODE JURISPRUDENCE · SCJ-NNN · N PAGES · SIGNIFICANT`.

- **outcome**: `"consumer"` | `"licensee"` | `"alternate_remedy"` | `"pending"` |
  `"none"` | `"split"`. Who succeeded on the electricity dispute, not CPC party
50→  role. A discom-petitioner who wins is `licensee`. Relegation to 6.5 / “apply
  under 4.4 in accordance with law” is `alternate_remedy`, not a consumer win.
  A direction that the connection *shall be granted* is `consumer`. Required
  from SCJ-301. Tally: `python tools/tally_outcomes.py UP-2005::4.4`.

- **headnote**: one dense paragraph stating the whole-case rule (the anchor when a case
  appears under several provision chapters).
- **facts**: 1–2 short paragraphs (about 80–180 words) of the story — who, the connection,
  what happened, what was challenged. Enough to follow the case; not the holding and not a
  dump of docket trivia. Rendered on the digest under the headnote as **FACTUAL SUMMARY**
60→  (cream box). Labels print as ordinary words (Headnote / Factual Summary), not letter-spaced.
- **holding_units[]**: `{provision, code, clause, topic, type, question?, holding,
  qualifier?, paras, flag?}`. Do **not** write `limiting_facts` (dropped from the digest;
  the story belongs in `facts`). `provision` is the key, e.g. `UP-2005::4.3(f)`, `EA2003::56(2)`,
  `WB-2004::5.2` (multi-state — key by the actual Code/Act, never merge a Code clause into an Act
  section). `type` = `"supply_code"` (green) for a Supply Code clause, `"interplay"` (grey) for a
  companion Act provision (s.56(2), s.126/127, s.46, s.174, tariff ss.61/62/64…). `flag` records a
  data-quality note (e.g. a litigant conflating a Code clause with an Act section) or transitional/
  multi-state scope. `paras` = judgment paragraph pins.
- **principle_tags[]**: `{tag, application, lead_authorities:[{name,docid}], paras}` — cross-cutting

import os
import tempfile

def atomic_write (path, text):
    d = os.path.dirname(path)
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".tmp_", dir=d)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(text)
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except:
        try: os.remove(tmp)

        raise

    cand = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".grok", "bin", "grok.exe")
    if os.path.exists(cand):
        return cand
    cand2 = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".grok", "bin", "grok")
    if os.path.exists(cand2):
        return cand2
    raise SystemExit("grok not found on PATH. Install Grok CLI or add %USERPROFILE%\\.grok\\bin to PATH.")


def run_logged(args: list[str], case_log: str, cwd: str = ROOT) -> int:
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PYTHONUTF8"] = "1"
    with open(case_log, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(f"$ {' '.join(args)}\n")
        f.flush()
        p = subprocess.Popen(
            args, cwd=cwd, env=env,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace",
        )
        assert p.stdout is not None
        for line in p.stdout:
            sys.stdout.write(line)
            f.write(line)
        return p.wait() or 0


def load_ticket_file(path: str) -> dict | None:
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)


def ticket_rel(cid: str) -> str:
    return f"supply-code/tmp/tickets/{cid}.json"


def json_exists(cid: str) -> bool:
    p = scj_queue.json_path(cid)
    return os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p) > 50


def next_seq() -> int:
    return int(scj_queue.load_state().get("next_seq") or 0)


def case_done(cid: str) -> bool:
    return scj_queue.case_is_done(scj_queue.load_state(), cid)


def prepare_claim(py: str) -> tuple[int, dict | None]:
    r = subprocess.run(
        [py, PREPARE, "--claim-new"],
        cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace",
    )
    if r.stdout:
        sys.stdout.write(r.stdout)
        if not r.stdout.endswith("\n"):
            sys.stdout.write("\n")
    if r.stderr:
        sys.stderr.write(r.stderr)
    if r.returncode == 2:
        return 2, None
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return r.returncode or 1, None
    ticket = load_ticket_file(scj_queue.TICKET_LEGACY)
    if not ticket or ticket.get("status") != "READY":
        return 1, None
    return 0, ticket


def author_one(ticket: dict, grok: str, py: str, case_log: str,
               max_turns: int | None) -> dict:
    """Write summaries/json/<cid>.json. Does not finalize."""
    cid = ticket["case_id"]
    tpath = scj_queue.ticket_path(cid)
    authoring = ticket.get("authoring") or "full"
    demoted = 0
    did_stencil = 0
    result = {
        "ok": False, "authoring": authoring, "demoted": 0, "grok": 0,
        "did_stencil": 0, "exit": 0,
    }
    if json_exists(cid):
        result["ok"] = True
        result["skipped"] = True
        return result

    if authoring == "stencil":
        code = run_logged(
            [py, STENCIL, "--write", "--ticket", tpath, "--force"],
            case_log,
        )
        if code == 0 and json_exists(cid):
            result["ok"] = True
            result["did_stencil"] = 1
            result["grok"] = 0
            return result
        code = run_logged([py, PREPARE, "--demote", "--ticket", tpath], case_log)
        ticket = load_ticket_file(tpath) or ticket
        authoring = ticket.get("authoring") or ""
        if authoring in ("", "stencil"):
            result["exit"] = code or 1
            return result
        demoted = 1
        result["authoring"] = authoring
        result["demoted"] = 1

    base_path = PROMPT_SHORT if authoring == "short" else PROMPT_FULL
    with open(base_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        base = f.read()
    out_json = ticket.get("out_json") or f"supply-code/summaries/json/{cid}.json"
    body = scj_queue.make_json_only_prompt(base, ticket_rel(cid), cid, out_json)
    prompt_path = scj_queue.write_worker_prompt(cid, body)
    turns = 50
    if max_turns is not None:
        turns = max_turns
    elif ticket.get("max_turns"):
        turns = int(ticket["max_turns"])
    grok_args = [
        grok, "--cwd", ROOT, "--prompt-file", prompt_path,
        "--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions", "--always-approve",
        "--max-turns", str(turns), "--output-format", "plain", "--no-auto-update",
    ]
    code = run_logged(grok_args, case_log)
    result["exit"] = code
    result["grok"] = 1
    result["ok"] = json_exists(cid)
    result["did_stencil"] = did_stencil
    result["demoted"] = demoted
    result["authoring"] = authoring
    return result


def finalize_one(ticket: dict, py: str, case_log: str, no_push: bool) -> int:
    args = [py, FINALIZE, ticket["case_id"], "--source", ticket["source"]]
    if no_push:
        args.append("--no-push")
    return run_logged(args, case_log)


def tail(path: str, n: int = 8) -> str:
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return ""
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            lines = f.read().splitlines()
        return " | ".join(lines[-n:])
    except OSError:
        return ""


def resume_tickets() -> list[dict]:
    state = scj_queue.load_state()
    out = []
    for t in scj_queue.open_tickets():
        cid = t.get("case_id")
        if not cid:
            continue
        if t.get("status") != "READY":
            scj_queue.delete_ticket(cid)
            continue
        if scj_queue.case_is_done(state, cid):
            scj_queue.delete_ticket(cid)
            continue
        out.append(t)
    return out


def parse_args(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--count", type=int, default=10)
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=2)
    ap.add_argument("--max-turns", type=int, default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--no-push", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--repo-root", default="")
    return ap.parse_args(argv)


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    repo = args.repo_root or ROOT
    os.chdir(repo)
    os.environ["PYTHONUTF8"] = "1"

    workers = args.workers
    if workers < 1:
        raise SystemExit("--workers must be >= 1")
    if workers > MAX_WORKERS:
        print(f"clamping --workers {workers} -> {MAX_WORKERS}", flush=True)
        workers = MAX_WORKERS

    py = sys.executable
    log_dir = os.path.join(SC, "tmp", "loop_logs")
    os.makedirs(log_dir, exist_ok=True)
    stamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_file = os.path.join(log_dir, f"next_case_loop_{stamp}.log")

    def L(msg: str) -> None:
        log(msg, log_file)

    grok = "grok"
    if not args.dry_run:
        grok = find_grok()

    L(f"Repo: {repo}")
    L(f"Grok: {grok}")
    L(f"Count: {args.count} | Workers: {workers} | MaxTurns: "
      f"{args.max_turns if args.max_turns is not None else 'ticket'} | "
      f"NoPush: {args.no_push} | Log: {log_file}")
    L(f"Starting next_seq={next_seq()}")

    if args.dry_run:
        L("DRY-RUN: claim under lock -> stencil or grok (JSON only) x workers")
        L("DRY-RUN: serial finalize_scj.py (Chrome/git/index)")
        return 0

    ok = 0
    fail = 0
    claimed = 0
    no_input = False
    prep_fail_streak = 0
    author_fail_streak = 0
    inflight = {}
    pending_finalize = []
    seq = 0

    resumes = resume_tickets()
    if resumes:
        L(f"RESUME {len(resumes)} open ticket(s): "
          + ", ".join(t["case_id"] for t in resumes))

    def submit_ticket(ex: ThreadPoolExecutor, ticket: dict) -> None:
        nonlocal seq, claimed
        seq += 1
        claimed += 1
        cid = ticket["case_id"]
        case_log = os.path.join(
            log_dir, f"case_{seq:02d}_{cid}_{stamp}.log"
        )
        tpath = scj_queue.ticket_path(cid)
        ticket["status"] = "AUTHORING"
        scj_queue.save_ticket(ticket, legacy=False)
        # keep READY on disk for crash resume (AUTHORING is open too)
        ticket["status"] = "READY"
        scj_queue.save_ticket(ticket, legacy=False)
        L(f"===== CASE {seq} / {args.count} | {cid} "
          f"authoring={ticket.get('authoring')} source={ticket.get('source')} "
          f"pages={ticket.get('page_count')} words={ticket.get('word_count')} "
          f"workers={workers} =====")
        fut = ex.submit(
            author_one, ticket, grok, py, case_log, args.max_turns
        )
        inflight[fut] = {
            "ticket": ticket, "case_log": case_log, "i": seq,
            "t0": time.time(), "tpath": tpath,
        }

    def try_claim(ex: ThreadPoolExecutor) -> None:
        nonlocal no_input, prep_fail_streak
        if no_input or claimed >= args.count:
            return
        if len(inflight) + len(pending_finalize) >= workers:
            return
        code, ticket = prepare_claim(py)
        if code == 2:
            no_input = True
            L(f"STOP: prepare reported NO_INPUT (next_seq={next_seq()})")
            return
        if code != 0 or not ticket:
            prep_fail_streak += 1
            L(f"FAIL prepare exit={code}")
            if prep_fail_streak >= 3:
                no_input = True
                L("STOP: prepare failed 3 times in a row")
            return
        prep_fail_streak = 0
        submit_ticket(ex, ticket)

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as ex:
        for t in resumes:
            if claimed >= args.count:
                break
            if json_exists(t["case_id"]):
                pending_finalize.append(
                    {"ticket": t, "case_log": os.path.join(
                        log_dir, f"case_resume_{t['case_id']}_{stamp}.log"
                    ), "i": claimed + 1, "t0": time.time(),
                     "author": {"ok": True, "authoring": t.get("authoring"),
                                "demoted": 0, "grok": 0, "did_stencil": 0}}
                )
                claimed += 1
                seq += 1
                L(f"RESUME-FINALIZE {t['case_id']} (JSON already present)")
            else:
                submit_ticket(ex, t)
        while len(inflight) < workers and claimed < args.count and not no_input:
            before = claimed
            try_claim(ex)
            if claimed == before:
                break

        while inflight or pending_finalize:
            while pending_finalize:
                item = pending_finalize.pop(0)
                ticket = item["ticket"]
                cid = ticket["case_id"]
                author = item.get("author") or {}
                elapsed = int(time.time() - item["t0"])
                fin_ok = False
                safety = 0
                if author.get("ok") and json_exists(cid):
                    if not case_done(cid):
                        safety = 1
                        L(f"JSON unfinalized; running finalize_scj.py {cid}")
                        fin_code = finalize_one(
                            ticket, py, item["case_log"], args.no_push
                        )
                        if fin_code != 0:
                            L(f"FAIL case {item['i']} {cid} finalize exit={fin_code}")
                            L(f"  tail: {tail(item['case_log'])}")
                            fail += 1
                            author_fail_streak += 1
                        else:
                            fin_ok = case_done(cid)
                    else:
                        fin_ok = True
                        scj_queue.delete_ticket(cid)
                if fin_ok:
                    L(f"OK case {item['i']} {cid} done -> next_seq={next_seq()} "
                      f"elapsed={elapsed}s")
                    L(f"  tail: {tail(item['case_log'])}")
                    ok += 1
                    author_fail_streak = 0
                elif not author.get("ok"):
                    L(f"FAIL case {item['i']} {cid} author json missing "
                      f"elapsed={elapsed}s")
                    L(f"  tail: {tail(item['case_log'])}")
                    fail += 1
                    author_fail_streak += 1
                try:
                    log_scj_review.append({
                        "event": "loop",
                        "case_id": cid,
                        "authoring": author.get("authoring") or ticket.get("authoring"),
                        "family": ticket.get("stencil_family") or "",
                        "source": ticket.get("source") or "",
                        "pages": ticket.get("page_count"),
                        "words": ticket.get("word_count"),
                        "citations": ticket.get("citation_count"),
                        "gate": ticket.get("gate") or "",
                        "elapsed": elapsed,
                        "ok": "1" if fin_ok else "0",
                        "safety_finalize": "1" if safety else "0",
                        "grok": str(author.get("grok") or 0),
                        "demoted": str(author.get("demoted") or 0),
                        "ik_citations": ticket.get("ik_citation_count"),
                        "text_citations": ticket.get("text_citation_count"),
                        "demoted_from": "stencil" if author.get("demoted") else "",
                    })
                except Exception:
                    pass
                if author_fail_streak >= 3:
                    L("STOP: 3 consecutive author/finalize failures")
                    no_input = True
                if not no_input:
                    try_claim(ex)

            if not inflight:
                continue
            done, _ = wait(list(inflight.keys()), return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED)
            for fut in done:
                item = inflight.pop(fut)
                try:
                    author = fut.result()
                except Exception as e:
                    author = {"ok": False, "exit": 1}
                    L(f"FAIL case {item['i']} {item['ticket']['case_id']} {e}")
                item["author"] = author
                pending_finalize.append(item)

    skipped = max(0, args.count - claimed)
    L(f"===== DONE ok={ok} fail={fail} skipped_remaining~{skipped} "
      f"next_seq={next_seq()} =====")
    L(f"Full log: {log_file}")
    try:
        subprocess.run(
            [py, os.path.join(ROOT, "tools", "log_scj_review.py"), "--summary"],
            cwd=ROOT,
        )
    except Exception:
        pass
    print(f"Summary: ok={ok} fail={fail} | next_seq={next_seq()} | log={log_file}",
          flush=True)
    return 1 if fail else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        sys.exit(main())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\nstopped; open tickets in supply-code/tmp/tickets/ will resume",
              flush=True)
        sys.exit(130)
"}

content:
The parallel pipeline is in place. The Sept 2 loop had already finished (SCJ-536 done, `input/` empty), so nothing racing it.

## What you run

Same command as before, now with workers (default **2**):

```
cd C:\Users\HP\Downloads\Grok\Claude
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\run_next_case_loop.ps1 -Count 50 -Workers 2
```

`-Workers 1` is the old one-at-a-time loop. Max is 4. Two PowerShell windows of this command are safe: they share a disk queue instead of fighting over one ticket.

## How it is split

| Stage | Parallel? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Claim (`prepare_next_scj.py`) | Serial, locked | Unique `SCJ-NNN`, one PDF per ticket |
| Author (stencil or `grok -p`) | **Yes, N workers** | Each grok writes only `summaries/json/SCJ-NNN.json` |
| Finalize (Chrome, index, git push) | Serial, locked | One git writer; `next_seq` never rewinds |

The old single file `tmp/NEXT_TICKET.json` is still written as a copy so chat **next** keeps working. Live work is `tmp/tickets/SCJ-NNN.json`. A crash leaves those tickets; the next start resumes them. A live worker owns a ticket by pid, so a second window will not steal it.

JSON quality is unchanged: each case is still a fresh `grok -p` with the same short/full prompt. Workers are told not to finalize, so they cannot collide on git.

## What not to do

Do not run chat **next** in this repo while an unattended loop is claiming. The lock protects ids; two authors on the same ticket is still wasted work.

There is nothing in `input/` right now, so a live run will print `NO_INPUT` and stop. Drop PDFs in, then start `-Workers 2`. On a typical 50 that should be about 90 min → 45–55 min.

42→### Windows pipeline (this checkout)

**User does nothing after starting it.** Chat **next** or the loop command both end in JSON + PDF + commit + **push** per case.

Token split:

1. `python tools/prepare_next_scj.py` — next unique PDF, skip dups, extract text, **reserve `SCJ-NNN`** (bumps `next_seq` under the queue lock). Per-case ticket at `tmp/tickets/SCJ-NNN.json`; legacy copy at `tmp/NEXT_TICKET.json`. Classifier may set `authoring=stencil` + `stencil_family`. Open tickets are skipped so two workers cannot take the same PDF. `--claim-new` skips resume (the parallel loop uses this).
2. JSON:
50→   - **Stencil** (`authoring=stencil`): `python tools/scj_stencil.py --write` — **no grok**, do not read the judgment. Live families: `6.5-billing-relegation`, `6.8-assessment-hearing`, `contempt-6.5-dismissed`. BILL cue includes `current`/`impugned` bill (SCJ-353), `wrong bill`, `electricity amount due`, unpaid electrical dues, recovery citation (SCJ-408). RELEGATE includes “should file a challenge” / “can get the bill corrected” / “if the petitioner approaches” (SCJ-399/468/487). GRANT veto: `we intervene` / `forthwith comply` / petition allowed / mandamus issued (SCJ-411). 6.8 is recovery citation + no hearing + deposit + Assessing Officer, pages ≤ 2; quash / s.135 stay off. Not stencil: listing-only, 4.4, 6.5 invoked-but-not-applied (SCJ-283/284/288), 6.5 order quashed (SCJ-379), 6.8 quashes (SCJ-367/375), court-grants.
   - **If stencil write fails:** `python tools/prepare_next_scj.py --demote` then follow the new `authoring` (short/full). **Do not** re-run prepare as stencil on the same id (358 burned 30 retries). Loop does this itself. Track `demoted`.
   - **Short path** if pages ≤ 2 **or** words ≤ 800, **or** uncited with pages ≤ 3 and words ≤ 1500 (`authoring=short`, `tools/prompts/next_case_short.txt`, `catalog_hits` on the ticket, max 15 turns). **Do not** load `catalog.txt`, SCJ-280, RUNBOOK, `finalize_scj.py`, or `gen_scj.py`. Schema is in the prompt. `paras` is a string; `not_decided` is objects. Uncited = fingerprint `citation_count` (IK hyperlinks **or** prose reporters / body `X v. Y`; not the caption or this case’s Neutral Citation No.).
   - **Full path** otherwise (`tools/prompts/next_case_once.txt` + catalog + SCJ-280).
   - Does not load this HANDOFF or `jurisprudence/index.json`.
3. `python tools/finalize_scj.py SCJ-NNN --source "<file>"` — schema gates, Chrome PDF (`--user-data-dir` required on Windows), state, spine, catalog, git commit+push. Takes the same queue lock as prepare. Never rewinds `next_seq` (inflight reservations stay reserved). Parallel workers do **not** run this; the orchestrator does, one case at a time.

- PDF name: `SCJ-<NNN>_<slug>.pdf` — **no `_Digest`**.
- Do not commit `extracts/SCJ-*.txt` / `.fp.json`.
- Linux Chromium path (`/opt/pw-browsers/…`) does **not** apply here.
60→
### Schema (still breaks `build_supply_code.py` if wrong)

1→# When the user says **next** / **next case**

Do **exactly one** unique pending judgment. Do not wait for confirmation. Do not start the treatise.

Unattended (user runs this; they do not babysit):

```
cd C:\Users\HP\Downloads\Grok\Claude
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\run_next_case_loop.ps1 -Count 50 -Workers 2
10→```

`-Workers 2` (default) authors two cases at once. Claim (id + PDF) and finalize (Chrome/git/index) stay serial under a lock, so two windows of this command cannot share an SCJ id. `-Workers 1` is the old one-at-a-time loop. Max 4. Do not run the old pre-queue script against the same `input/` while this is going.

content:
Pushed to `claude/supply-code-jurisprudence-design-yiwgen`. GitHub is now the queue.

**On the branch**
- `supply-code/input/2024/` — **215** pending PDFs (~25 MB)
- `supply-code/processed/2024/` — the **9** dups already in the corpus
- Finalize now stages `input/…` deleted and `processed/…` added, so the PDF is not left in both trees
- Removed the year-folder `.gitignore` that was hiding those PDFs from git (`*` ignore). `input/2025/` still has that file; drop it when you add 2025 to GitHub the same way

**From another folder later**

That folder must be a clone of this repo, on this branch. Grok CLI, Python, and Chrome still run **on that machine**.

```
git clone https://github.com/aharish-dot/Claude.git <folder>
cd <folder>
git checkout claude/supply-code-jurisprudence-design-yiwgen
git pull
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\run_next_case_loop.ps1 -Count 50 -Workers 2
```

If the clone already exists: `git pull`, then the same loop command. Drop new year folders into `supply-code/input/` on GitHub (or commit them from any clone), pull, run.

Run **one loop at a time**. The lock is local to the working tree. Two clones processing together will fight on `git push`.

**Tokens vs time**

| | Change |
|---|---|
| **Grok tokens** | None. Same extract, same short/full/stencil prompts. GitHub storage is not model usage. |
| **Authoring time** | None. Still local grok + Chrome. |
| **Git time** | One-time: this ~25 MB push (already done, ~13s). A new clone pays that once on `git pull`. After that, each case commit is a **rename** of a blob that is already on GitHub, plus the small JSON/digest — often *less* upload per case than before, when `processed/` PDFs were new blobs. |
| **Repo size** | +~27 MB now. The PDF is stored once (input, then processed). Not doubled. |

Extracts stay local and gitignored. JSON, digest PDFs, state, catalog, and the judgment PDFs stay on GitHub.
